scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A few drops of glue can hold two things together forever. Why does glue stick, but not to the inside of its bottle?

scenes.name: flow
scenes.text: Liquid glue flows into tiny cracks and bumps on a surface, that look smooth to us.

scenes.name: forces
scenes.text: Up close, glue molecules are attracted to the surface molecules. This is called adhesion.

scenes.name: harden
scenes.text: Then it hardens. Some glues dry as water or solvent evaporates, others cure through a chemical reaction.

scenes.name: cohesion
scenes.text: Once hard, the glue holds strongly to itself too. That inner strength is called cohesion.

scenes.name: bottle
scenes.text: In the bottle, white glue can't dry, because the water can't evaporate, and the plastic is hard to stick to.

scenes.name: superglue
scenes.text: Super glue is different. It reacts with tiny traces of moisture in the air and on surfaces, and sets in seconds.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Flow in, grab on, harden, hold. Follow for more on how things really work.
